answer: No—not by itself. A recorded supervision event or completed reconciliation may evidence an activity, but does not establish its adequacy, the correctness of the underlying ownership rights, or compliance throughout the relevant period. Those conclusions require an applicable legal standard and facts showing that the activity and its results satisfy that standard. The retained provisions supply relevant requirements and considerations, but no rule making either event conclusive proof of fulfillment.

claims.inference: Paragraphs 10 and 11 distinguish continuing responsibility from the substantive condition of the records and arrangement. It follows that proof of an isolated activity does not alone establish either requirement's fulfillment.
missing_premises: Applicability of the retained edition to the entity, product, activity and assessment period, including relevant authorisation conditions and modifications.
An applicable interpretation of operational soundness and proper ownership records, and evidence satisfying it over the relevant period.
claims.proposition: Retained responsibility and proper ownership records require more than proof that supervision or reconciliation occurred.

support.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

claims.inference: For outsourced valuation, the text requires a qualitative standard of care and continuing oversight. A supervision entry establishes neither the quality nor continuity of that oversight. Extending this valuation-specific provision to other tokenisation services requires a separate legal justification.
missing_premises: The UT provision applies, the entity is the management company, and the third party performs scheme valuation.
Evidence of the third party's relevant knowledge, experience and resources.
Evidence of supervision's scope, frequency, competent review, findings, escalation and follow-up across the period.
A justified assessment that these facts meet reasonable care, skill and diligence and the ongoing supervision and periodic review requirements.
claims.proposition: A recorded supervision event does not by itself establish adequate supervision under UT 6.11C.
claims.status: Conditional deduction from an expressly limited provision

support.quote: Where a third party is engaged in the valuation of a scheme, the management company shall exercise reasonable care, skill and diligence in the selection, appointment and ongoing monitoring of such third party in ensuring such entity possesses the appropriate level of knowledge, experience and resources that commensurate with the appropriate valuation policies and procedures for each scheme.
The valuation activities of such third party should be subject to ongoing supervision and periodic review by the management company.

claims.inference: The Appendix treats regular reconciliations as one consideration alongside legal validity and encumbrances. Agreement between records cannot alone establish that either record correctly represents enforceable ownership. The proposed factual checks below are evidentiary requirements for that inference, not an express statutory checklist.
missing_premises: Which records legally determine ownership and settlement finality under the product documents and governing law.
The reconciliation's actual scope, coverage, timing, inputs and results, rather than merely a completion flag.
Evidence that discrepancies were investigated and appropriately resolved, and that reconciliations recur as required.
Evidence connecting token balances and holder identities to valid product interests, including relevant encumbrances.
A justified standard for record accuracy, completeness and currency, and evidence that it was met.
claims.proposition: A completed reconciliation is relevant evidence but is not conclusive proof of proper ownership records.

support.quote: For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

For example, whether the ownership interest of the underlying assets of the Tokenised Securities are legally valid under the applicable governing laws, whether there are regular reconciliations between the records for the extrinsic rights and the records for the distributed ledger tokens, or whether any encumbrance affects the extrinsic rights.

claims.inference: Register maintenance has a specified actor and is distinct from Product Provider responsibility. Its applicability and regulatory effect must be established before using it as an assessment standard; the word 'must' does not independently establish statutory liability.
missing_premises: The scheme type and identity of the scheme, trustee or trustee-appointed register keeper.
Applicable authorisation conditions, modifications or relaxations.
Evidence that the relevant holder register was actually maintained properly throughout the assessment period.
claims.proposition: UT 6.8 may supply an additional register-maintenance requirement, but cannot automatically be assigned to every Product Provider.

support.quote: The scheme, or in the case of a unit trust, the trustee or the person so appointed by the trustee must maintain a register of holders.
This UT Code does not have the force of law.

The Commission may modify or relax the application of a requirement in this UT Code if it considers that, in particular circumstances, strict application of the requirement would operate in an unduly burdensome or unnecessarily restrictive manner.

rival_readings: An allocation-focused reading of paragraph 10 asks whether ultimate responsibility remains with the Product Provider despite outsourcing. That narrower conclusion does not establish adequate supervisory conduct or proper records under paragraph 11.

A conduct-focused reading asks whether the Product Provider exercised appropriate oversight; an outcomes-focused reading asks whether operations and records were substantively sound. A combined reading requires both. The retained text does not establish a complete discharge test or make one recorded event sufficient under any of these readings.
unresolved: No actual supervision or reconciliation evidence is supplied; neither fulfillment nor breach can be determined.
The applicable qualitative standard, assessment period, actor roles and product-specific conditions remain unproved.
Good outcomes alone do not necessarily prove adequate oversight; documented oversight alone does not prove proper outcomes.
The supplied computational results concern formal representations and declared semantics. They do not establish the legal standard, applicability, factual adequacy or legal truth.
